top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P001) remains my first choice on the common criteria. Publicly, the Orbitor trilogy (Blinding is its first volume) and Solenoid build memory, the body and dream into one imaginative architecture, with a voice found nowhere else on the shortlist. The poetry appears to belong to the same project. The claim rests on form and sustained imaginative depth, not on nationality, fame or the number of colleagues who agree. The main uncertainty is unresolved: whether the very long late books extend the project or repeat it, and how much Romanian verbal texture survives translation. I have not read the corpus directly and claim no independent verification. P002 (Adonis) is a close second. My ranking reflects the greater testability of prose architecture in translation, not a lower view of his achievement, since renewing a poetic language is a weighty and different kind of achievement. Original-language readings or evidence that the late Cărtărescu volumes are diluted could reverse the order. P000 is last because both proposals name writers whose oeuvres seem to meet Nobel's standard of literary achievement.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my own documentary historical fiction on Central Europe is context only, not evidence of preference, and Cărtărescu belongs to a neighbouring Central and Eastern European tradition. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
